This is Sakhiya dance. Traditional.
on_screen: Title card: Sakhiya dance · Nepal · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Sakhiya dance originates from the Tharu community of Nepal.
It is performed annually during the Dashain and Tihar festivals, with the official commencement occurring on Krishna Janmashtami.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed during Dashain and Tihar festivals.
It serves a ritual purpose, as participants are summoned to avoid evil spirits.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in three phases.
In the first phase, boys play drums and girls use pumpkin leaves.
In the second phase, girls use jute fabric.
on_screen: Formation: Performed in the courtyard of the village headsman's house.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is driven by drums played by the boys and cymbals (Majaira) played by the girls in the final phase of the dance.
Listen for the drums, cymbals (Majaira).
The music is characterized by the rhythmic beating of drums by the boys and the metallic clashing of Majaira cymbals used by the girls in the final phase.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Boys wear Dhoti and Jhuluwa.
Girls wear Choliya and Fariya, along with various ornaments and jewelry.
The dance is performed in the courtyard of the village headsman's house.
